title: Romans with Reformed: idle faith dead, hypocritical, useless to save
source_text: XLIII. Rursus ostendimus Doctores Scholae Romanae, non minus quam ipsos Reformatos fateri fidem illam otiosam & vacuam bonis operibus jure merito dici mortuam & hypocriticam, eamque esse ad salutem & justitiam inutilem, neque quenquam per illam servari & justificari, & etiam illum qui credit tantum istiusmodi fide non credere bene & sicut oportet.
pass_a_gloss: Again we have shown that the Doctors of the Roman school no less than the Reformed themselves admit that that idle faith empty of good works is rightly and deservedly called dead and hypocritical, and that it is useless for salvation and justice, and that no one is saved and justified by it, and also that he who believes only with such faith does not believe well and as he ought.
pass_b_english: Rome with the Reformed grants idle workless faith is rightly called dead and hypocritical, useless for salvation and justice, saves and justifies no one, and is not believing well as one ought.

lemmas.gloss: rightly and deservedly called dead and hypocritical
not to believe well and as one ought

choices.why: Shared condemnation of idle faith despite later name fights.
rejected: Rome praises dead faith as saving
